data.narrative:
Cambium is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Simon Waddington and Stephan Herrera that has raised $127M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 9 comparable companies—1 public and 8 private—operating in the same sector and stage, including Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Divergent, and Exotec.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy for post-money valuation, applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding an implied value of $241M. Peer-median analysis across three directly comparable Series B robotics companies—Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B)—produces a median valuation of $1.8B with a range of $1.6B to $2.0B.

The two methods produce materially different signals. The stage-progression approach suggests $241M; the peer-median approach indicates $1.8B. A triangulated range spanning both methods yields a low of $205M, median of $996M, and high of $2.0B. The wide dispersion reflects two core uncertainties: whether Cambium's operational metrics and growth trajectory align with higher-valued peer cohorts, and whether the stage-progression method—which anchors to historical capital deployed—adequately captures recent market pricing in frontier robotics. Resolution requires detail on revenue run-rate, unit economics, and competitive positioning relative to named peers.
